entities.summary:
Bridget of York was the seventh daughter of King Edward IV and his queen consort Elizabeth Woodville, born around 1480 in Pontefract, Yorkshire, England. As a member of the powerful Woodville family, Bridget's life was shaped by the tumultuous politics of the Wars of the Roses and the subsequent reign of her half-brother Edward V.


 Bridget's marriage to Thomas St. Barrell, a distant cousin, produced at least eight children, including a son who would go on to inherit his father's titles and lands. Her family's fortunes rose and fell with the fortunes of the Tudor dynasty, as she became a lady-in-waiting to King Henry VIII's wife, Catherine of Aragon.


 Despite her relatively minor role in the royal court, Bridget's legacy extends to her descendants, who would go on to play significant roles in English history, including the Earl of Pembroke, who would lead the charge against the Spanish Armada in 1588.


 Bridget of York's life serves as a poignant reminder of the complex web of alliances, rivalries, and power struggles that defined the medieval period, where the lines between loyalty, duty, and ambition were constantly blurred.
